content.text: {"id": "mm6218a2", "data_focus": {"v": "yes", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control were lowest among Mexican-Americans (68.7%, 58.7%, and 35.5%, respectively)"}]}, "outcome_types": [{"v": "binary/categorical", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control were lowest among Mexican-Americans (68.7%, 58.7%, and 35.5%, respectively)"}]}], "analytic_depth": [{"v": "summary", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "less than 60% of those with stage 2 hypertension were treated with medication"}]}, {"v": "comparison", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control were lowest among Mexican-Americans (68.7%, 58.7%, and 35.5%, respectively)"}]}, {"v": "stratified/adjusted", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "Among those with stage 2 hypertension, blacks had greater awareness (77.6%) compared with whites (65.7%) and Mexican-Americans (66.0%)"}, {"loc": "table 2", "q": "Prevalence of selected characteristics among adults aged ≥18 years with uncontrolled hypertension"}]}], "study_design": [{"v": "cross-sectional", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "NHANES is an ongoing, stratified, multistage probability sample of the noninstitutionalized U.S. civilian population."}]}], "methods_quotes": [{"loc": "text", "q": "All analyses were performed using statistical software to account for sampling weights and adjust variance estimates for the complex sampling design."}, {"loc": "text", "q": "A univariate chi-square test of independence was used to determine statistically significant (p<0.05) differences across racial/ethnic groups."}, {"loc": "text", "q": "Because multiple NHANES cycles were combined, trends over time could not be examined, and prevalence estimates could not be age adjusted."}, {"loc": "note", "q": "§ Pearson chi-squared statistic, corrected for survey design."}], "confidence": "medium", "uncertain_fields": ["analytic_depth"]}
